description: A cleaning company uses a cleansing chemical and odor-removing chemical to clean a house. Each unit of the cleansing chemical takes 4 units to be effective while each unit of the odor-removing chemical takes 6 minutes to be effective. The company must use at least 100 units of the cleansing chemical. In total, at least 300 units of chemicals can be used per house. Further, because the cleansing chemical is strong, there can be at most twice the amount of cleansing chemical as odor-removing chemical. How many units of each should be used to minimize the total time it takes for a house to be cleaned?

CleansingChemicalTime.definition: Time it takes for one unit of cleansing chemical to be effective

OdorRemovingChemicalTime.definition: Time it takes for one unit of odor-removing chemical to be effective

MinCleansingUnits.definition: Minimum number of units of cleansing chemical to be used per house

MaxTotalUnits.definition: Maximum total number of chemical units used per house

MaxCleansingToOdorRatio.definition: Maximum ratio of cleansing chemical units to odor-removing chemical units

objective.description: "Minimize the total time required to clean a house using cleansing and odor-removing chemicals"

constraints.description: The number of units of cleansing chemical used must be at least MinCleansingUnits
The number of units of cleansing chemical used must be no more than MaxCleansingToOdorRatio times the number of units of odor-removing chemical used

description.Description: The total number of chemical units used (cleansing plus odor-removing) must be at least 300 units per house.

cleansingUnits.definition: Number of units of cleansing chemical used per house

odorRemovingUnits.definition: Number of units of odor-removing chemical used per house
